audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Tahm Kench Levels 2 and 3 and the 2+ items row, while whys[2] and whys[3] describe Levels 3 and 4-5 as Swain's zone-control window.
audit.why: The mirror audit set the chart to Skill / Skill / Swain / Swain / Tahm Kench / Tahm Kench / Skill and rewrote its reasoning to match. Rows 1, 2, 3 and 6 are brought into line here, and they agree with this page's own prose as well as the 57.59% win rate.
audit.corrected: Level 2 to Skill, Level 3 and Levels 4-5 to Swain, 2+ items to Skill — all as matched full/content pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] calls Level 6 'a guaranteed win for you' in every extended fight.
audit.why: Devour has no cooldown of its own — it gates on three stacks of An Acquired Taste and 100 mana. So a Tahm Kench who has been chipping you through the trade can swallow you in the middle of Demonic Ascension whenever the stacks are up. 'Guaranteed' is exactly the word that gets a player killed at the moment the page tells him he cannot lose.
audit.corrected: The drain outpaces Thick Skin, but strip or avoid the three stacks first, because Devour ends the drain outright.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (P An Acquired Taste, R Devour cd 0 cost 100)

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fields have Tahm Kench devouring HIMSELF — wants.foe[0] 'Absorb your E root into a self-W devour', wants.you[1] 'the moment he tries to devour himself out of a losing trade', and content.mid 'he cannot devour himself mid-drain without burning W on a three-second cooldown'. The same sentence also attaches a 3-second cooldown to W.
audit.why: Devour is his R and is cast on a champion — 'dealing magic damage if they are an enemy, or shielding them if they are an ally'. He cannot eat himself. His W is Abyssal Dive, a 1000-range dive that knocks up, on 21s. The 3-second cooldown belongs to Thick Skin (E), which converts stored damage into a shield. So the page has the wrong ability in the wrong slot with the wrong cooldown, three times, and it teaches the player to wait for an escape move that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Thick Skin is the shield on 3s; Abyssal Dive is the 21s engage knockup; Devour is cast on a champion, and against you it is the tool that ends your drain.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (W Abyssal Dive range 1000-1200 cd 21/20/19/18/17, E Thick Skin cd 3, R Devour text)

audit.whatIsWrong: Tongue Lash is called 'His stun' in four fields with no condition attached, and the shield is called a 'grey-health passive' throughout.
audit.why: Riot's text: Tongue Lash 'damages and slows the first unit hit... Applies a stack of An Acquired Taste to enemy champions. If the champion already has 3 stacks of An Acquired Taste, they are stunned and the stacks are consumed.' It reaches 900 on a 7s rank-1 cooldown and is a slow until the third stack. That is countable — you can trade at one or two stacks and disengage before the third — and 'dodge his stun' throws that away. The grey health is likewise Thick Skin's stored-damage shield, an active he chooses to spend, not a passive that ticks on its own.
audit.corrected: Count An Acquired Taste stacks: Tongue Lash slows at one and two, stuns and consumes at three. Thick Skin is a spent shield, not passive grey health.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (Q text, range 900, cd 7/6.5/6/5.5/5; P; E text)

audit.why: report[8] already carries anti-heal early, which covers the flagged needs-antiheal interaction (Tongue Lash heals him, Thick Skin heals out of combat). No edit needed.

edits.after: Tongue Lash stuns only at three stacks — else it slows.

edits.after: Cash Thick Skin's stored damage into a shield as your root lands, so the pull combo hits the shield and not his health

edits.after: Toggle R after Thick Skin is spent — on a 3s cooldown the shield is only as big as the damage you already dealt

edits.after: Build three An Acquired Taste stacks, then Tongue Lash for the stun and Devour you out of your own drain

edits.after: Demonic Ascension drains faster than Thick Skin restocks — but at three stacks Devour swallows you mid-drain, so strip them first.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are a grinding zone-control phase: your W eye has enough range that Tahm Kench cannot walk toward you without eating damage through his grey health, and every root-pull sequence nets you a Soul Fragment that permanently grows your health pool. The danger here is his Q tongue stun — if he lands it at close range he can slow your fragment collection and potentially engage a short trade where his grey-health bulk wins; always W first to force him to decide whether to stand in the eye or step into root range. At Level 6 your R Demonic Ascension is the fight-ender: activate it the moment a trade extends past the first exchange and drain through his grey health faster than his passive can restock it — he cannot devour himself mid-drain without burning W on a three-second cooldown, and that window is your kill window.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are a grinding zone-control phase: your W eye has enough range that Tahm Kench cannot walk toward you without eating damage through Thick Skin, and every root-pull sequence nets you a Soul Fragment that permanently grows your health pool. The danger here is Tongue Lash — it reaches 900 and stuns only once he holds three An Acquired Taste stacks on you, so count the stacks and break off at two rather than guessing; always W first to force him to choose between standing in the eye or stepping into root range. At Level 6 your R is the fight-ender: activate it the moment a trade extends past the first exchange and drain faster than Thick Skin can restock — but Devour is cast on a champion, not on himself, so at three stacks he swallows you out of your own drain. Spend the stacks first.

notes: The self-devour error appears three times and is the worst thing on this page: it invents an escape move Tahm Kench does not have, attaches Thick Skin's 3s cooldown to Abyssal Dive, and leaves the player waiting for a window that never opens. All three fields are corrected. MIRROR DIVERGENCE at Level 6: the mirror audit flipped that row to Tahm Kench, but this page's whys[4] and spikes[1] both argue Swain owns it, and I did not reverse prose I believe is mechanically right — the honest version is that Demonic Ascension does outpace Thick Skin and Devour is what takes the row back, which is now stated. Level 6 is left as Skill here; see questionsForUser.
